segments.text: You are going to listen to a talk giving advice to students who are traveling to the UK for study.
First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16.
Now, listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16.
Good afternoon, young ladies and gentlemen.
Welcome back to the orientation session for those of you who are going to spend your last year of college in the UK
as part of our exchange program.
In the morning, you were told about the academic things you need to know. Now,
I'm going to give you some tips before you head off to a new country. What I'm
about to say is accumulated from my own experience and from those who have gone
through this before you. Please save your questions until the end of the talk.
Thank you. Right, before I give you any specific advice about traveling and
living in a brand new environment,
make yourself a checklist of all the things you need to do and take with you,
including the tips I'm going to give you now,
especially if you are very forgetful. Even if you're not,
it's still a good idea to have one to keep things in order. All right.
Now about things to bring along,
I'm sure each of you must already have things in your mind to put in your
baggage, but you might decide to leave some behind after listening to me.
I'm not going to talk about the obvious documents, like your visa or passport, which are essential
for your departure.
The first category I'm going with is more essential for the first few weeks, food.
In the past, there were many students bringing as many as three suitcases just for food.
Of course, we can argue that we can't eat Western food, but there are many restaurants
that serve various types of dishes and many supermarkets that sell ingredients to make
your own favorite meal.
From my own perspective, just bring as much as you need for your first week when you're
settling down, not for the whole month.
You can always expect help from the local community, they are very friendly and helpful.
Now about clothing.
Just like food, bring enough to wear for the first week or two in case your house's
washing machine has a problem. After that, 90% of the clothes you brought will surely
be forgotten in your suitcase or your wardrobe. Why? Well, there are several reasons. First
is fashion. As you know, clothing trends change over time, and you can find plenty of high
quality garments there in the city you're going to live in. Second is price. For the
same piece of clothing, it's actually cheaper to buy it there than here in our country.
Lastly, and most importantly, is durability. The weather conditions in the UK are completely
different from where we live. Thus, the clothing sold there is made to withstand the local
climate. The clothes you bring along might not be durable enough for a long time, and
And you'll have to buy new ones eventually.
So why not get your new clothes sooner?
For medicine, you should only bring ones that are critical to your medical condition.
Other common drugs for minor ailments can be obtained for free at the school's medical
center.
If you bring your own drugs, you're expected to show relevant medical documents, like a
prescription at the airport.
And you might need it to refill your bottle at the chemists.
Now you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.
Now listen carefully and answer questions 17 to 20.
That's quite enough for the traveling part.
Now to the living.
First things first, it's easy for young people like you, especially when you enjoy yourself
too much living abroad for the first time, to lose contact with your family.
Try to call your parents at least once a day in the first week so they know you're
settling in well.
Then you can reduce the frequency to at least once a fortnight.
You don't know how much your loved ones miss you.
If you have signed up for a slot in the Hall of Residence, it's perfect.
But if you decide to rent a room outside, remember to choose one close to a bus stop
because that will be your main means of transport in the city.
Many might want to live near the supermarket, but it's not like you're going out for groceries
every day, right?
For those of you who love shopping, don't forget to join the student's union and get
a member card.
It's what will get you discounts on your shopping bill, not your normal student card.
At the time you arrive, the city will also have its biggest event of the year, the Balloon
Festival, which attracts people from all over Europe.
Don't miss it.
Well, I think that's enough for today.
Now, any questions?
That is the end of section 2.
You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to section 2.
Now turn to section 3.
